instruction: Create persistent namespace with bind mount
Use unshare to persist net namespace
Use nsenter with path to namespace file
Run a full container with busybox and unshare
Minimal container using unshare and pivot_root
output: unshare --mount --pid --fork --mount-proc bash -c 'mkdir -p /newroot && mount -t tmpfs tmpfs /newroot && mkdir -p /newroot/{bin,proc} && cp /bin/busybox /newroot/bin/ && pivot_root /newroot /newroot/oldroot && exec chroot . /bin/busybox sh'

instruction: Use nsenter to debug pod networking
Check network namespace of Kubernetes pod
output: crictl inspect $(crictl pods --name mypod -q) | jq '.info.runtimeSpec.linux.namespaces[] | select(.type == "network")'
nsenter -n -t $(crictl inspect $(crictl pods -q | head -1) | jq '.info.pid') ip addr
nsenter -t $(crictl inspect $(crictl ps --pod $(crictl pods --name nginx -q) -q) | jq '.info.pid') -a /bin/bash
systemctl show --property MainPID sshd | cut -d= -f2 | xargs -I{} ls -la /proc/{}/ns/

instruction: Run systemd service with network namespace

output: systemctl show myapp.service -p PrivateNetwork -p PrivateTmp -p PrivateDevices

instruction: Run with all systemd sandboxing options
output:
cat > /etc/systemd/system/sandboxed.service << 'EOF'
[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/secure-app
PrivateTmp=true
PrivateNetwork=true
PrivateDevices=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=true
NoNewPrivileges=true
EOF
